page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The architecture includes 1.0 thread per core, a 32 MB L3 cache, and support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7a.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, software compilation via Clang, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks also ranks in the top tier, while large block read and write bandwidths fall within the strong category. Database operations and Redis SET operations show strong to top-tier throughput, with Redis reaching 122.99 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds are strong to top-tier for prompt processing and text generation on small to medium models, though large 70B model prompt processing drops to average.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or hardware-accelerated parallel processing. However, its high physical core density and DDR5 memory speed make it qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy general-purpose workloads. It is suited for software compilation, database operations, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
